steps.body: Read the picture backward: a square made from two matching triangle halves can be separated along its diagonal seam into those two triangles.
steps.narration: Read the picture backward: a square made from two matching triangle halves can be separated along its diagonal seam into those two triangles.

widget.prompt: A square is cut along one diagonal. Tap the shape each piece becomes.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: Each piece is only half the square, with three sides rather than four.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: A diagonal cut leaves a slanted edge, giving three sides, not four.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A straight cut cannot produce a curved edge.

widget.missFeedback: Follow the diagonal cut and count the sides of one piece.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — one straight diagonal cut turns a square into two triangles.

predict.prompt: The two triangles are pushed back together. What shape returns?
predict.reveal: Composing undoes decomposing, so the original square comes back.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s decompose.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

widget.prompt: A rectangle was built from two equal squares side by side. Which pieces can you recover by opening the middle seam?

options.label: Into two squares
options.feedback: Correct — opening the middle seam recovers the two equal squares used to build the rectangle.

options.label: Into nothing — it is one piece
options.feedback: Any shape can be cut into smaller shapes; being one piece now does not prevent it.

options.label: Into a circle
options.feedback: Straight cuts produce straight edges, so a round piece cannot appear.

options.label: Into a cube
options.feedback: A cube is a solid; cutting a flat shape leaves flat pieces.

steps.body: Read the picture forward again: the same two triangle pieces rejoin to rebuild the square. Composing and taking apart undo each other here.
steps.narration: Read the picture forward again: the same two triangle pieces rejoin to rebuild the square. Composing and taking apart undo each other here.

widget.prompt: Two matching triangle halves are pushed back together along their long edges. Tap the shape that returns.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: One piece is a triangle, but both matching halves together rebuild the square.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: These are the two matching halves cut from a square, so rejoining them returns that square.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: Straight triangle edges cannot make a curved circle. They rebuild the square.

widget.missFeedback: The pieces came from a square. Rejoin the matching long edges to rebuild it.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — rejoining the matching triangle halves rebuilds the square.

widget.prompt: A square made from two matching triangle halves is separated along the seam. How many corners does one triangle piece have?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole square's corner count, not just one triangle piece; count only the corners on one half.
That misses one corner; the seam adds a new corner where the diagonal cut meets each side.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

widget.prompt: Which action reverses joining two equal squares along a middle seam?

options.label: Open the middle seam
options.feedback: Correct — opening the seam reverses the join and recovers the two equal squares.

options.label: Erase the whole shape
options.feedback: Erasing does not take the built shape apart into its original pieces. Open the seam instead.

options.label: Round every outside edge
options.feedback: Changing the outside edges does not reverse the join. Open the middle seam to recover the squares.

options.label: Fold it into a cube
options.feedback: Folding changes a flat shape into a solid; it does not recover the two flat square pieces.
